title: CPU- and GPU-initiated Communication Strategies for Conjugate Gradient Methods on Large GPU Clusters
problem: Conjugate Gradient methods have low computational intensity and high communication sensitivity, limiting scalability
motivation: GPU-accelerated solvers need efficient communication strategies for multi-GPU clusters with thousands of GPUs
method: They develop iterative solvers (like Conjugate Gradient, which solve equations by successive approximations) that overlap computation with data movement across large GPU clusters. Instead of routing all GPU-to-GPU data through the CPU, they use direct communication libraries (NCCL/RCCL for collective operations, NVSHMEM for direct memory access) that let GPUs exchange data efficiently. They test two variants: one where the CPU initiates data transfers, and one where GPUs initiate them directly.
key_novelty: The core idea is letting GPUs directly initiate data transfers using NVSHMEM, removing the CPU bottleneck that had to coordinate all communication in the cluster.
contributions: Scalable CG and pipelined CG implementations
